speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) other than the SG Fresh Produce Label, what efforts are in place to increase demand for locally grown produce; and (b) how many local companies have successfully applied for the label.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: To complement the ramp-up in local food production under the "30 by 30" goal, my Ministry supports the local farmers in a few ways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Last year, we ran the Singapore Food Story campaign to raise consumer appreciation and support for local produce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: As part of the campaign, the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) launched the SG Fresh Produce (SGFP) logo to help consumers identify and support local produce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: The logo was designed in consultation with industry stakeholders and over 2,200 members of the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: SFA is also helping to promote local produce through promotions and better branding and display at major retailers like NTUC FairPrice, Cold Storage, Sheng Siong and Prime Supermarket.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: As part of its outreach, SFA has helped to connect farms with potential corporate buyers, such as food and beverage and retail establishments, to negotiate possible offtake arrangements and partnerships.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: This certification recognises local farms that have adopted resource-efficient farming practices and ensured clean farming environments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: It serves as a mark of assurance to our consumers that the produce from these farms are not only free from synthetic pesticides, but are also grown in a sustainable way.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: In the spirit of Singapore Together, the Ministry for Sustainability and the Environment and SFA convened a Citizens’ Workgroup last year to co-create ideas to increase demand for local produce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: While SFA will continue to support local farmers through promotions and initiatives mentioned above, increasing demand for local produce is ultimately the responsibility of the farmers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Producing good quality and safe farm products, giving good value to the consumers and getting production at a competitive cost level will ensure the sustainability of our local farming industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Mr Desmond Tan) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: We will work closely with the farmers and the stakeholders to help local produce gain market acceptance in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think many appreciate the fact that we are tackling food security and note that we have a "30 by 30" goal.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But there are concerns that as we ramp up production and improve productivity, whether there is also an equal focus on and resources being put towards ensuring and monitoring that production is environmentally sustainable.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To that end, I am glad to hear about the upcoming "Clean and Green" standard and also the work of the Citizens' Workgroup.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But, for example, practices such as proper waste management, how will that be looked into?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would be very grateful if the Ministry could share some of its plans in this regard.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And also to what extent is food from land-based and sea-based farms exported for consumption overseas instead of being consumed here in Singapore, and does that go towards our "30 by 30" goal?

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: There are actually two parts to the question.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The first is on how, as we ramp up, we continue to ensure that environmental sustainability is taken into account.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: So, I would touch on the first part, first.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Through the process of masterplanning, we can, not just increase the productivity of our produce, but also to take into account some of the environmental factors in the design of the land use as well as the methods in which the farming technology can be introduced in this new plan.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: To give you an example, as part of the design of the Lim Chu Kang masterplanning, we will be taking into consideration the possibility of integrating different services together, as a shared service, for example, the waste management that the Member talked about.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: This will allow us to ensure that the environment factors are taken into account and to pool the resources together from different farming industries and technology to be introduced to ensure that the environment is protected.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Having this hub also allows us to ensure the integration of some of the services from the food waste to industry feed and food feed or vegetable feed.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: At the same time, the solid waste from poultry waste can also be used as fertilisers for the vegetables.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: These are some of the ideas that we will be implementing and this gives us an opportunity not just to ramp up the productivity but also to ensure that environmental sustainability will be taken into account.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: The second part of the question is about exports.

speaker: Mr Desmond Tan
text: Today, most of our local produce are catered towards local markets.
